name: AWS - Full IAM Account Dump & JMESPath Querying
command:
aws --profile <profile> iam get-account-authorization-details --filter User Group LocalManagedPolicy Role | tee account-auth-details.json
aws --profile <profile> iam get-account-authorization-details --filter User --query "UserDetailList[].UserName"
description: When a compromised IAM user has iam:GetAccountAuthorizationDetails (part of SupportUser, SecurityAudit, ReadOnlyAccess managed policies), dump the entire IAM structure in one API call: all users, groups, roles, and managed policies with their attached policies and group memberships. The --filter flag limits to specific resource types. Use --query with JMESPath syntax to extract specific fields from the JSON output — avoiding large JSON blobs and piping to jq.
source: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 24: Enumerating AWS Cloud Infrastructure (24.5.2, 24.5.3)

examples.label: Full IAM dump - all users, groups, roles, policies
examples.command: aws --profile target iam get-account-authorization-details --filter User Group LocalManagedPolicy Role | tee account-auth-details.json

examples.label: Account-wide summary (total users, groups, policies, MFA state)
examples.command: aws --profile target iam get-account-summary | tee account-summary.json

examples.label: List all users in the account
examples.command: aws --profile target iam list-users | tee users.json

examples.label: List all groups
examples.command: aws --profile target iam list-groups | tee groups.json

examples.label: List customer-managed policies (only attached ones)
examples.command: aws --profile target iam list-policies --scope Local --only-attached | tee policies.json

examples.label: JMESPath - extract all usernames as a flat list
JMESPath - get details of a specific user
JMESPath - filter users whose name contains 'admin'
examples.command: aws --profile target iam get-account-authorization-details --filter User --query "UserDetailList[?contains(UserName, 'admin')].{Name: UserName}"

examples.label: JMESPath - get admin users and admin groups in one query
examples.command: aws --profile target iam get-account-authorization-details --filter User Group --query "{Users: UserDetailList[?Path=='/admin/'].UserName, Groups: GroupDetailList[?Path=='/admin/'].{Name: GroupName}}"

examples.label: Read a specific custom policy document (workaround if direct access denied)

notes: iam:GetAccountAuthorizationDetails is a single read-only API call that returns the ENTIRE IAM configuration. It is included in AWS-managed policies like SupportUser (iam:Get*, iam:List*), SecurityAudit, and ReadOnlyAccess. The response can be very large (MB range for large orgs) — always pipe to tee to save a local copy. --filter accepts: User, Group, Role, LocalManagedPolicy, AWSManagedPolicy. JMESPath syntax: [] = project array items; [?field=='value'] = filter; {Key: field} = reshape; [*].field = extract field from all items. The --query flag processes the response client-side (not server-side) — the full API call always runs. If GetAccountAuthorizationDetails is denied but list-users/list-groups/list-policies/list-policy-versions/get-policy-version are allowed, assemble the picture manually (see aws-iam-scope-permissions).

references.title: OffSec PEN-200 - Enumerating AWS Cloud Infrastructure

recommended.note: Verify iam:Get*/List* permissions before attempting the full dump.

defense.why_it_works: IAM enumeration maps the entire access control surface of an AWS account — all users, groups, roles, policies, and their attachments. With iam:Get*/iam:List* permissions, an attacker discovers: other IAM users and their permissions, roles assumable by the current principal, overprivileged policies, and privilege escalation paths (iam:CreatePolicyVersion, iam:AttachUserPolicy, iam:PassRole, etc.). This is the cloud equivalent of AD enumeration.
defense.prerequisites: AWS credentials with iam:List* and iam:Get* permissions. AWS CLI configured. Sufficient permissions to call IAM APIs (often available by default to developers).
defense.impact: T1087.004 Account Discovery: Cloud Account + T1069.003 Permission Groups Discovery: Cloud Groups. Maps all IAM principals and their permissions — identifies privilege escalation paths, over-permissioned roles, and lateral movement targets within the AWS account.
defense.detection:
CloudTrail: iam:ListUsers, iam:ListRoles, iam:ListPolicies, iam:GetPolicy, iam:GetPolicyVersion in rapid succession from a single principal. GuardDuty: 'Discovery:IAMUser/AnomalousBehavior'. These calls are normal for IAM admins but unusual for developer credentials calling hundreds of IAM APIs in minutes.
Processes performing local or domain account enumeration by invoking account directory queries or security APIs followed by structured output of account lists (DET0587/AN1612).
Suspicious shell commands or unauthorized access to /etc/passwd or /etc/shadow (AN1613).
Directory service queries or system utilities accessing account metadata stores, producing enumeration output (AN1614).
Cloud provider API calls where principals retrieve IAM users or roles in rapid succession (AN1615).
ESXi host account configuration or management APIs queried to retrieve user account listings (AN1617).
defense.artifacts: CloudTrail: bulk iam:List*/iam:Get* API calls | GuardDuty: IAM discovery anomaly | CloudWatch metric: unusual IAM API call volume from single principal
defense.prevention:
Least-privilege IAM policies: developers should NOT need iam:List* on all resources. IAM permissions boundary: restrict what actions any role can perform even if over-permissioned. SCPs: deny iam:List* except for IAM admin roles. CloudTrail alerting: SIEM rule on bulk IAM enumeration. Use aws-nuke or permission boundary enforcement.
Operating System Configuration: Prevent administrator account enumeration via UAC (GPO: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\CredUI\EnumerateAdministrators).
User Account Management: Manage creation, modification, use, and permissions associated with user accounts.
defense.evasion: Enumerate slowly (rate-limited calls over hours). Enumerate only necessary targets (specific users/roles) rather than full account dump. Use pacu with --delay between calls.
defense.misconfiguration: Developer IAM policies include iam:List* and iam:Get* for '*' resource. No CloudTrail alerting on bulk IAM API calls. No IAM permissions boundaries. SCPs not used to restrict IAM actions.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Overpermissive developer policy:
# {
#   'Effect': 'Allow',
#   'Action': ['iam:List*', 'iam:Get*'],
#   'Resource': '*'
# }
# → Developer can enumerate all IAM — maps escalation paths

# No SCP restriction:
aws organizations list-policies-for-target --target-id ACCOUNT_ID --filter SERVICE_CONTROL_POLICY
# → No SCP limiting iam:List* = any account member can enumerate
defense.secure_config:
# Least-privilege: developers don't need iam:List* on *
# Restrict to their own user:
# {
#   'Effect': 'Allow',
#   'Action': ['iam:GetUser', 'iam:ListAccessKeys'],
#   'Resource': 'arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT:user/${aws:username}'
# }

# SCP denying iam:List* for non-admin:
# {
#   'Effect': 'Deny',
#   'Action': ['iam:List*', 'iam:Get*'],
#   'Resource': '*',
#   'Condition': {'StringNotEquals': {'aws:PrincipalArn': 'arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT:role/IAMAdmin'}}
# }

# CloudWatch alarm on bulk IAM calls:
# Metric filter: $.eventSource=iam.amazonaws.com AND $.errorCode='' (successful)
# Alarm: > 50 IAM calls in 5 minutes from same principal → SNS alert
